doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dorothy's role and how Lloyd chooses where to play
summary: Newton praises Dorothy; Lloyd says they have lawyers and people to handle business and that he accepts only correct invitations.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Now let me ask you: In the sixties I know that you were very blessed. I see it...
Don’t pull no punches. If you got something funny to ask me, bring it.
No, no. I have to acknowledge that because I greatly appreciate...

I greatly appreciate... She’s an incredible human being, an incredible artist. I have nothing but the highest respect for her, and it’s beautiful to see the relationship that the two of you have together.

Well I learned from my grandfather. We have lawyers, we have people. You know, if someone comes at us right, fine! I’ll take an invitation, you know, if it’s correct. And they put us... See how I live? I’m not gonna go and live in... I could live in a castle or a chicken shack, but I’m not adverse to - I’m not gonna deal with polarity. I mean, if that’s the condition of the condition, I can eat very humble food, you know, and do. But when I go out to play they have to, you know, make it correct. I don’t go all the time. But I’m going out now for a month, playin’ I don’t know how many concerts. She knows. But I don’t even know all the places I’m going. I know we start in Sweden and it moves around, you know. I’m happy to say that I’m blessed that I’ve lived to where some people know that I’m bringing something, you know. But those who said to me that you’re not... what’d they say?
You had to start at the back of the line.
